c.tagline: The 'Queen of the Dolomites,' a glamorous alpine resort hosting the 2026 Winter Olympics

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for mountain refuges

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €5 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and higher than most Italian towns given the resort setting

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number; mountain rescue is reached via 112

walk: Central Cortina and Corso Italia are compact and walkable; the surrounding peaks, lakes, and ski lifts require a car, bus, or cable car

safety.crime: Minimal crime; main risks are mountain/weather-related for hikers and skiers

hood_landmark.Tofana / Freccia nel Cielo: The Tofana cable car ('Arrow in the Sky') base
hood_landmark.Cinque Torri: The Cinque Torri via ferrata and WWI trenches
hood_landmark.Passo Falzarego: Passo Falzarego's mountain pass and cable car

hood_desc: The elegant pedestrian core with boutiques, cafes, and the basilica; the natural base for any visit.
A cable car base a short walk from the center, accessing one of Cortina's classic ski and hiking areas.
The dramatic Tofana cable car, one of the most scenic lift rides in the Dolomites, reaching over 3,200m.
A striking rock formation area southwest of town, popular for via ferrata climbing and WWI history.
A high mountain pass west of town with cable car access and refuges, a gateway to more remote Dolomite trails.
lodging: Cristallo, a Luxury Collection Resort & Spa

water.note: Alpine tap water is excellent and safe to drink.

transit.sys: Dolomiti Bus regional network and cable cars/gondolas serving the ski areas
transit.pay: Tickets and lift passes sold at kiosks and lift stations
transit.note: A car is useful for reaching more remote trailheads, though the town center is very walkable

transport.air: Venice Marco Polo Airport (VCE), about 2 hr away; Innsbruck Airport (Austria) is a further alternative
transport.train: No direct rail to Cortina; nearest stations are Calalzo di Cadore or Dobbiaco, connected by bus
transport.bus: Dolomiti Bus and seasonal coaches connect to Venice, Belluno, and Innsbruck
transport.car: Well connected via the SS51 highway; winter driving in the Dolomites requires snow tires/chains

airport.name: Venice Marco Polo Airport
airport.transport: Shuttle bus/transfer, train plus bus, or rental car

net.m: Good 4G/5G in town, patchier at altitude
net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: A TIM, Vodafone, or WindTre tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for mountain guides
tip.r: A cover charge (coperto) is common instead of tipping; rounding up is a nice gesture

landmarks: Tofana di Mezzo and the Freccia nel Cielo cable car
The 'Arrow in the Sky' lifts visitors to 3,244 meters atop Cortina's third-highest Dolomite summit for a staggering 360-degree panorama.
Cinque Torri
Five freestanding rock towers ringed by restored WWI trenches form an open-air war museum and one of the Dolomites' most photogenic hiking playgrounds.
Lago di Sorapis
A demanding but beloved trail leads to this glacial lake of unreal milky turquoise, cupped beneath the spires of the Sorapis group.
Tre Cime di Lavaredo
The three colossal rock teeth that symbolize the Dolomites rise a scenic drive from Cortina, circled by the range's most famous half-day hike.
Corso Italia
Cortina's chic pedestrian promenade parades boutiques, galleries, and grand hotels beneath the bell tower, the social catwalk of the 'Queen of the Dolomites'.
Lagazuoi and its WWI tunnels
A cable car from Passo Falzarego reaches this front-line summit, where restored Great War tunnels burrow through the rock beneath a superb rifugio terrace.
Passo Giau
The Dolomites' most photogenic mountain pass unfurls hairpins beneath the lonely pyramid of Ra Gusela, a magnet for cyclists, skiers, and photographers.
Basilica dei Santi Filippo e Giacomo
Cortina's 18th-century parish church anchors Corso Italia with its slender 70-meter campanile, the town's defining silhouette against the Tofane.
Lago di Misurina
A romantic mirror-lake reflecting the Sorapis and Tre Cime, ringed by a lakeside promenade and grand belle-époque facades twenty minutes from town.
Cascate di Fanes
Within the Dolomiti d'Ampezzo Natural Park, the Fanes torrent hurls itself through a wild canyon in a chain of waterfalls reached by forest trails.

train.note: Cortina has had no railway since the Calalzo-Cortina-Dobbiaco line closed in 1964 - its trackbed is now the Lunga Via delle Dolomiti cycle path. The nearest stations are Calalzo di Cadore, about 35 minutes south by bus, and Dobbiaco/Toblach to the north, both on Trenitalia (https://www.trenitalia.com) regional lines; a rail link is under discussion ahead of future Olympic events but nothing is running.

bus.note: No international coaches. Cortina Express (https://www.cortinaexpress.it/) and ATVO run direct coaches from the bus terminal to Venice Mestre and Marco Polo airport in about two hours, and Dolomitibus (https://dolomitibus.it/) covers Calalzo, Belluno and the Dolomite passes. Winter services are much heavier than summer ones, and passes can close in snow.

ferry.note: Cortina sits at 1,200 m in the Dolomites with no navigable water, so there are no ferries of any kind.

half.name: Bolzano
half.blurb: South Tyrol's capital, a bilingual Alpine city home to Ötzi the Iceman and a mix of Italian and Austrian culture.

half.name: Alpe di Siusi (Seiser Alm)
half.blurb: Europe's largest high-altitude alpine meadow, with sweeping views of the jagged Dolomite peaks beyond.

half.name: Lake Dobbiaco
half.blurb: A turquoise glacial lake at the foot of the Dolomites, ringed by an easy lakeside walking path.

full.name: Venice
full.blurb: The canal city of St. Mark's Square and the Grand Canal, reached by a scenic drive down from the Dolomites.

full.name: Innsbruck
full.blurb: A mountain-ringed Tyrolean capital with a medieval old town and the gilded Golden Roof landmark.
